open_points.subject: OWNER_FORM_FIELDS inter-module contract
open_points.text: The generated code reads the table, so the data provider's constant delivers it (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1), as it delivers the seven tables of M22–M28; a `models` catalog of the same table would not reach the code, and none is declared.
open_points.question: Which logical module owns and exports `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS`, which modules are its callers, and may each caller rely on the table for rendering fields, reading submitted fields, or both?
options: One owner-interface module imports the constant and owns both rendering and request reading.
Separate renderer and request-reader modules each consume the constant directly.
A facade consumes the constant and supplies derived field information to renderer and request-reader modules.
open_points.default_guess: Make the data-provider module the sole owner and have each module that directly renders or reads owner fields consume the constant explicitly.

witness.initial: A later release adds a valid row to OWNER_FORM_FIELDS for a new owner field.
events: The owner opens the affected page.
outcomes: An implementation treats the table as authoritative for both rendering and reading, so the new field is shown and its submitted value is read.
An implementation lets only the request reader use the table while the renderer retains its own field list, so the new field is accepted in principle but is never shown to the owner.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the released field is available on the page.

open_points.text: The generated code reads the table, so the data provider's constant delivers it (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1), as it delivers the seven tables of M22–M28; a `models` catalog of the same table would not reach the code, and none is declared.
open_points.question: After State 5 names the owning provider and semantic consumers, how will the exact direct imports of `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` be represented?
options: Declare a direct `module_internal` edge from every module that names `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` to its provider.
Declare one facade consumer of `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` and pass derived values to modules that do not name the constant.
Place rendering and request reading in one consumer module with one direct provider edge.
consequences: The dependency graph precisely exposes every direct consumer but may contain several provider edges.
The dependency graph is smaller, but the facade needs an explicit later-layer contract for the derived information.
The import graph is simplest, but rendering and request reading become coupled in one module.
open_points.requirement: The generated code reads the table, so the data provider's constant delivers it (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1), as it delivers the seven tables of M22–M28; a `models` catalog of the same table would not reach the code, and none is declared.
open_points.default_guess: Declare the constant only for modules that name it directly, using complete and minimal `module_internal` edges.
